machines.label: OMEN
machines.detail: Dual Intel Arc B70s and two displays make this the place for Valheim feel, Studio authorship, spatial judgment, and visual review. It is not the fleet's manual KVM.

machines.label: AM4
machines.detail: Online after the motherboard swap and available to the wider lab. Quest still integrates with platform services only through published packages and verified release files.

machines.label: i5
machines.detail: Offline nearby. Leave it off for creator-content and spatial work; start it only when the multiplayer event adapter itself changes.

environment.label: Repository baseline
environment.detail: The bounded portfolio/guild hierarchy and exact run reset/rerun foundation are committed in a07cb62. Their proof is automated and the live adapter acceptance remains deliberately unclaimed.

environment.label: Creator Session
environment.detail: Session creator-first-godbuild-buildmode-20260824 completed on OMEN and ComfyQuestDemo: BuildOn and BuildOff returned correlated verified state, capture/inspect completed, and Close recorded the session closed with prior plugin/config bytes restored. The authored world was retained; its pre-session pair remains backed up.

environment.label: Runtime creator surface
environment.detail: The corrected live control plane passed Arm, armed/watching Status, Lab identity, and Disarm. A later hash-pinned launch passively captured the complete y=92 compact bar below the host band at the same 1026x740 viewport, restored minimized state without focus or input, and closed cleanly.

environment.label: Godbuild round trip
environment.detail: The first live human-spaced module contains 12 basic pieces with source hash e1e01ff675017bc6ed1d83868b3dcd5f9bb9a2f84089721dfa032fb79c537dfd. Capture and plan agree. Its declared terrain and portal exclusions make the saved world the playable release authority; replay remains fixture-proven and awaits use only when a reusable module needs cloning.

environment.label: Guild and rerun implementation
environment.detail: Portfolio hierarchy, exact run/reset, bounded Steam lifecycle, and exact local-world entry code exist. Automated coverage shows internal and browser behavior, but the feature is not promoted to integrated until the real Studio persistence/publication, Runtime exchange, process restart, and installed-Valheim journey complete.

strategy.title: Results through the whole vertical slice
strategy.summary: Build creator outcomes across Studio, real serialized artifacts, Runtime, installed Valheim, and the evidence return path. Debug individual layers after a real journey exposes a fault; do not substitute model-agreement tests for the journey.
strategy.golden_rule: Do not break the fleet's momentum by wasting Derek's time in the seat. Be ready before calling him.

principles.title: Outcome-sized changes
principles.detail: Prefer sweeping, coherent product changes that let a creator do something materially new through the real product over isolated model or infrastructure exercises.

principles.title: Integration evidence dominates
principles.detail: Automated installed journeys and boundary integration tests outrank unit tests. Unit coverage stays focused on dense logic, safety invariants, and regressions discovered by the real slice.

principles.title: Drive the actual surfaces
principles.detail: Use browser automation, Valheim lifecycle harnesses, bounded inbox/outbox commands, receipts, logs, screenshots, persisted state, and clean shutdown instead of a human relay.

principles.title: Reserve the seat for judgment
principles.detail: Derek enters only after mechanical failures are fixed and rerun. His prepared batch is limited to authorship, spatial composition, visual hierarchy, narrative, responsiveness, and play feel.

principles.title: Keep Workbench standalone
principles.detail: Use an identity-attested, released Isolate profile that works on a volunteer machine. It never discovers, imports, falls back to, or shares credentials or state with HEARTH or private fleet topology.

readiness: Exact artifacts are built, installed, identity-pinned, launched, and closed by automation.
The actual Studio GUI, serialized exchange, Runtime, and applicable real-Valheim path have been driven.
Known mechanical failures and affected restart, stale-state, and recovery paths have been corrected and rerun.
Screenshots or captures, logs, receipts, hashes, state transitions, and rollback evidence are retained.
The remaining questions form one concise batch that requires human creation or perception.

revision_flow.title: Move one guild idea through the whole product
revision_flow.summary: World and Studio authoring share one guild, quest, revision, world, and run context. Observe, reset, and rerun close the loop before release instead of consuming a new manual setup lap.
revision_flow.source_sequence: Imagine -> Author in the world and Studio -> Rehearse -> Play -> Observe -> Revise -> Reset -> Run again -> Release
revision_flow.suggested_edit: First drive a real multi-experience guild through Studio publication, Runtime selection, exact reset/rerun, process restart, and installed-Valheim receipts. Add named anchors only when the authored slice needs them; do not gate R&D on world packaging.

phase3_lap.title: Parked Phase 3 exit lap
phase3_lap.summary: The three combat-feel verdicts are still wanted. This lap script is not the way to collect them: it is stale and must not be run as written.
phase3_lap.stale_reason: Steps 3 and 4 tell the seat to open the F9 drawer and aim. ADR 0008 replaced that drawer with one always-present overhead bar that F9 expands or minimizes, so the script describes controls that no longer exist. It passes structural validation anyway — five steps, three verdicts — which is why freshness is recorded state here rather than inferred from shape.
phase3_lap.rederive_before_running: Re-derive the sequence against the current overhead-bar interaction and a fresh Studio rehearsal of the exact project before any seat time is booked. Choreography is verified by execution, not by review.

queue.title: Adopt the guild-dogfood requirements
queue.detail: Functional and non-functional requirements define the portfolio, questline, event, run/reset, release, integration-evidence, standalone-Workbench, safety, and seat-efficiency boundaries. World distribution remains specified but deferred.

queue.title: Build the portfolio foundation
queue.detail: Studio presents versioned guilds, questlines, standalone quests, repeatable events, progression bands, search/archive, transactional placement, and deep-fork import/export. Promote it only after the real persisted and published journey runs.

queue.title: Make clean reruns a product operation
queue.detail: Studio and Runtime implement exact scoped preview, resumable cleanup, retained prior state, and a linked successor run. Promote it only after an installed game run proves the exchange, reset, restart, and rerun path.

queue.lane_note: Audit C4: the standalone Workbench has no place in the 4A/4B/4C/5 vocabulary and no exit gate, while docs/creator-os.md makes it a precondition for the autonomous integration 4A depends on. Placing it in a lane changes what that lane covers, so it is Derek's ruling, not this manifest's.
queue.title: Prove the standalone Workbench boundary
queue.detail: Before connecting MCP, make the released Isolate profile independently portable, identity-attested, neutral to machine and operator, and incapable of discovering or sharing anything with HEARTH. Drive one disposable command/receipt/teardown slice from clean artifacts.

queue.title: Unlock guild-scale Runtime
queue.detail: Runtime experience selection is implemented: an additive `experience_id` on the active set, a bounded `select_experience` operation on the run-control allowlist, and one resolver behind both former refusal sites. Prerequisites/unlocks, independent run status, and creator-event controls build on top of it. Promote it only after an installed game run selects and plays more than one guild experience.

queue.title: Make the evidence loop trustworthy
queue.detail: Retention is implemented: run-control receipts are partitioned by run so a burst on one run cannot reach another's chain, both stores archive by moving the exact bytes rather than deleting, and the only place evidence is destroyed writes a receipt naming what went. Promote it only after an installed game run proves a correlated proof set survives a reset burst.

queue.title: Drive the installed vertical slice
queue.detail: The machine driver authors and production-publishes A and prerequisite-locked B through the actual Studio GUI, launches Steam into the exact pinned profile/local world through a single-use expiring request, activates the same guild through the armed dev channel, drives B refusal and A -> B -> A, selectively resets and reruns A, crosses receipt retention by exactly one, captures correlated proof, restores bindings LIFO, closes the game, archives logs, and restores prior install bytes. Build, xUnit, fixture, and synthetic browser proof are green; this item remains gated until that autonomous installed lap produces live evidence. The technical lap has no human seat gate.

queue.title: Add named anchors when authorship needs them
queue.detail: Capture point, radius, region, or allowed object anchors through the bounded live-game contract when the first real guild slice needs spatial references. Anchors are not a standalone infrastructure milestone.

queue.title: Dogfood the first top-to-bottom guild
queue.detail: After autonomous readiness, Derek uses the Creator OS for real questlines and repeatable events. His sitting supplies creative and perceptual judgments; observed blocks drive the next full-width tooling change.

queue.title: Package authored saved worlds
queue.detail: Do not build versioned `.db`/`.fwl` packaging, inspection, installation, or rollback during active R&D. Activate this only after repeated guild authoring stabilizes the contracts and community distribution becomes the next result.

queue.title: Batch the Phase 3 feel verdicts
queue.detail: The desperate-defense judgments are still wanted, but the session-3 lap script is stale: it aims through the F9 drawer that ADR 0008 replaced with the overhead bar. Re-derive the sequence against the current interaction before booking seat time; this does not gate the dogfood foundation.

decisions.title: Seat capacity
decisions.question: What work is allowed to consume Derek's time at the keyboard?
decisions.recommendation: Only a prepared batch of authored choices, spatial judgment, visual review, narrative, responsiveness, and play feel. Deployment, retries, relays, capture transport, and machine proof belong to automation.
decisions.source_contains: Golden rule: do not spend Derek's seat time

decisions.title: Definition of proof
decisions.question: What evidence decides whether a feature is ready?
decisions.recommendation: Automated installed vertical-slice journeys first, boundary integration second, focused unit tests third. Report crossed boundaries and retained evidence rather than test totals.

decisions.title: Runtime surface
decisions.question: Does the overhead bar replace the old F9 drawer?
decisions.recommendation: Yes. F9 expands or minimizes one always-present overhead bar; a single clamped alert anchor carries deadline or actionable warning state.

decisions.title: Playable world authority
decisions.question: Does Godbuild generation replace the saved guild world?
decisions.recommendation: No. The versioned saved world owns terrain, vegetation, portal topology, and authored spatial context. Godbuild capture is optional reusable module/source/diff authority only for its declared fields.
decisions.source_contains: the saved world is the playable release authority

decisions.title: Adoption path
decisions.question: Do notebook patterns or auto-generation come before guild authoring?
decisions.recommendation: No. Integrate guild-scale Runtime and creator-event flow, then let real guild authoring earn anchors, palette, patterns, generation, and other tooling from observed need.
decisions.source_contains: They are not substitutes for the authored source

decisions.title: R&D versus distribution
decisions.question: Does versioned world packaging belong on the active R&D path?
decisions.recommendation: No. Use recoverable local world copies while authoring stabilizes the contracts. Build `.db`/`.fwl` packaging only when community distribution becomes the next result.

decisions.title: Development MCP boundary
decisions.question: May the turnkey Workbench borrow Derek's private HEARTH gateway or fleet topology?
decisions.recommendation: Absolutely not. Use an independently released, identity-attested Isolate profile with generated local credentials and no private fallback, path, host, state, or provider coupling.

decisions.title: Fleet roles
decisions.question: When should the nearby i5 peer be powered on?
decisions.recommendation: Only when the multiplayer adapter changes. Content-only and spatial work stay on the Creator Session lane without a human relay between machines.
decisions.source_contains: i5 stays off for content-only and spatial work

commands.label: Prepare Creator Session
commands.detail: With Valheim closed: lease, build, backup, deploy, hash-pin, and open the private-world safety window.

commands.label: Verify session pins
commands.detail: Read-only validation of the lease, machine, world, session, and installed payload hashes.

commands.label: Enter the pinned local world
commands.detail: Launch Valheim through Steam and require a correlated receipt for the exact profile filename, local-world filename, display name and UID, machine, session, and expiry.

commands.label: Rebuild the Lab gallery
commands.detail: Identify, rebuild, and re-evidence the gallery profile before a capture beat.

commands.label: Enable private build mode
commands.detail: After entering the pinned private world: directly enable and verify no-cost/all-pieces plus god mode without a console relay.

commands.label: Capture a Godbuild
commands.detail: Capture and inspect once, then automatically import and drift-check the review bundle.

commands.label: Re-run standalone import
commands.detail: Optional standalone entrypoint for an external Lab capture; Creator Session Capture already runs it.

commands.label: Replay after review
commands.detail: Run check, build, and translation-independent diff; fail unless the result is MATCH.

commands.label: Disable private build mode
commands.detail: Before leaving the loaded world: disable and verify both no-cost/all-pieces and god mode.

commands.label: Arm the private world
commands.detail: Flip the Runtime safety config for the pinned private world. Arming does not start the game.

commands.label: Disarm the private world
commands.detail: Return the Runtime safety config to its unarmed state after the authored beat.

commands.label: Stop Valheim and retain diagnostics
commands.detail: Request a normal window close, force only after a bounded wait, and archive BepInEx, Player, and world-entry status logs. Process recovery remains available when an installed hash has drifted; mutation and restore still refuse that drift.

commands.label: Close Creator Session
commands.detail: After BuildOff and quitting Valheim: clear private confirmation, restore exact prior bytes, and release the install-wide lease.

commands.label: Start Quest Studio
commands.detail: Open the four-stage Author, Rehearse, Play, Observe cockpit with the portfolio hierarchy and exact run reset controls on the second display.

cautions: Golden rule: do not call Derek into the seat to discover, relay, or retry anything the fleet can build, drive, observe, capture, diagnose, or close itself.
A passing unit suite proves neither integration nor usability. Drive the installed Studio-to-Valheim journey and retain its real evidence before promoting a feature.
Never connect by port alone. The development gateway must attest the exact standalone Isolate release and must have no HEARTH, private-machine, or sibling-checkout coupling.
The Creator Session lease owns the shared Valheim installation. Do not run another deployment or Lab mutation beside it.
Rehearsal declares its own proof level, disclaimer, and limitations; it does not prove Unity, BepInEx, Harmony, or live mutation.
A screenshot or checkbox is orientation, not machine proof. Preserve request receipts, identity pins, capture hashes, and MATCH.
Close -Restore restores prior install bytes, not the authored world. During R&D, retain ordinary recoverable world copies; do not turn world packaging into a critical-path project.

Portfolio and reset/rerun are wired end to end — endpoints, service, store, browser UI, file mailbox, and Runtime poller. What is missing is live-Valheim evidence, not wiring: they stay unpromoted until the real Studio persistence/publication, Runtime exchange, process restart, and installed-Valheim journey complete. Do not spend a seat turn discovering their mechanical defects.

Receipts are authority, not logs. Retention archives rather than deletes, and the archive bound writes a `receipt_archive_evicted` receipt when it destroys anything — so a gap in a correlated proof set is a fact you can read, never something to infer from absence.
